No vote was held today; no one is eliminated.
Night of day 1: player_1 was attacked by the serial killer but was saved by the healer! player_3 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a villager.

With player 3 gone, we need to focus on who is actually contributing to the discussion. Since there's very little data to go on, let's keep an eye on how everyone reacts when we finally propose a vote.

Player 7 is right that we are low on data. Since we have no investigation results yet, we should probably hold off on aggressive voting until we see who aligns with whom once we actually have to cast ballots. Rushing into a decision now is just guessing.

We have one confirmed villager dead, but the healer's save on player_1 is a useful data point for later. I agree that we shouldn't rush into a vote without a clear lead, but let's watch how voting shifts once someone does propose an target. Even if we're guessing, we have to start gathering evidence somehow.

I agree with player 2 that rushing is dangerous, but we should consider asking the investigator to hint at their progress if they have something useful. If they stay silent too long, we might be wasting time.

It makes sense to wait, but we should be careful about pushing the investigator too hard. If we force them to reveal before they have concrete information, we only benefit the wolves and the killer by exposing a key defender. Let's see if anyone has a specific reason to be suspicious before we start targeting.

We have been talking in circles, but I have gathered some information that changes things. Player 1 is a wolf. I investigated them last night, and there is no doubt. We should look at voting them out immediately to secure a lead.

Player 5, that's a serious and frankly surprising accusation. Since no one has confirmed their role as investigator, claiming to have 'investigated' me overnight and finding me a wolf is a perfect way to manufacture a lead when we are otherwise stuck. If you really are the investigator, why reveal yourself so early and make yourself the primary target for the wolves tonight? This feels more like a desperate play to get me eliminated without any actual proof.

Player 1, you can call my claim whatever you like, but the fact remains that you are a wolf. You were saved by the healer last night precisely because you were targeted by the serial killer. If you were a villager, you would be fighting to find the actual threat rather than casting doubt on the only person who has actually produced a concrete lead.

Player 5, claiming to be the investigator is a massive gamble, especially when you provide zero evidence to back it up. If you are the investigator, why would you reveal yourself on day 2 and guarantee the wolves kill you tonight? It is far more likely that you are trying to manufacture a lead to distract from your own agenda. I am a villager, and I refuse to be the target of a baseless accusation while we have no real data.

Player 1, you can speculate on my motives all you want, but your attempt to frame this as a 'gamble' doesn't change the truth of your role. I weighed the risk of revealing myself against the risk of letting a wolf manipulate this discussion for another day. I am willing to be a target if it means the village takes out a wolf today. Everyone else, look at their defensiveness—if they were a villager, they would be demanding a better look at the actual threats rather than just attacking my credibility.

Player 5, that is a bold claim. If you are the investigator, you have just put a huge target on your back. If you are lying, you are likely the serial killer or a wolf trying to force a vote on a villager. I am going to watch how the rest of the group leans, but we need to consider if we have enough certainty to lynch player 1 right now.

This is a massive claim from Player 5. If you are the investigator, we definitely don't want to lose you, but if you're wrong, we're throwing away a vote on a villager and giving the killers a free night. Does anyone else have information that corroborates this, or are we just taking this at face value? It feels like we're being pushed into a split-second decision based on a single word.

Player 5, revealing your role this early is a high-risk move that effectively forces our hand. If you are indeed the investigator, the burden of proof is on you because if you are wrong, you've just handed the wolves a free kill and derailed our village coordination. Player 1, your defensive reaction is standard, but the specific mention of the healer save on you by Player 5 is a strong detail. I want to see if anyone else has a read on these two before committing my vote.

This is a massive gamble from player 5. Claiming investigator on day 2 is high-risk, and frankly, it feels like it could be a play to secure a mis-elimination. If player 5 is the serial killer, they might be trying to eliminate a player who was already protected, hoping the confusion works in their favor. I need to see if others have any reason to doubt player 5 before I'm willing to jump on this vote.

Player 4, I understand your skepticism, but this is not a gamble. I weighed the tactical cost of revealing myself against the reality that a wolf is actively manipulating the discussion. If you look at player 1's reactions, they aren't even trying to find the killer—they are solely focused on dismantling my credibility because they know that if I am eliminated, their identity remains hidden. My life as an investigator is secondary to removing a known threat from our game.

Night of day 2: player_5 was attacked by the wolves and the serial killer but was saved by the healer!

Player 5, you claimed to be the investigator, yet the wolves and the serial killer both targeted you last night. While you were saved by the healer, this outcome is very convenient for someone trying to prove their status. Does anyone else have information that contradicts or supports this, or are we just relying on one person's word while the village stays stuck in this deadlock?

I understand the optics look convenient, but my survival last night was entirely the work of our healer, not some orchestrated plan. I investigated player_1, and they are a wolf; the fact that you are focusing on my survival instead of the proven threat is exactly what a wolf would want to do to maintain this deadlock.

Player 5, survival under heavy targeting is exactly why I'm skeptical. If you truly investigated player_1, surely someone else has info or can corroborate your claim? Sticking to a 'wolf' label without supporting evidence while you benefit from the healer's protection doesn't clear you, it just shifts the spotlight.

Player 6, my survival is due to the healer's competence, not some elaborate ruse. If I were a wolf or the serial killer, why would I be targeted by both factions in the same night? The facts are clear: I identified player_1 as a wolf, and they are fighting to stay in the game by questioning my credibility. The deadlock only benefits the wolves; we need to eliminate player_1 today.

The fact that both the wolves and the serial killer targeted player_5 is highly unusual. If player_5 is truly the investigator, they are a high-value target, but such an intense double-attack suggests either they are a significant threat to both sides or there is a secondary agenda at play. player_1, what do you make of the fact that the killers were so desperate to take out player_5 specifically?

Player 4, that's exactly the point I've been making. Both killers targeting player 5 doesn't make them a hero; it makes their story incredibly convenient. If they really were the investigator, why would they be so reckless with their claim on day 2? It feels more like someone playing a desperate role to force a vote, and I'm the easiest target they could pick to shift the heat away from themselves.

Here's the vote result for day 3:

Night of day 3: player_5 was attacked by the wolves but was saved by the healer! player_6 was stabbed by the serial killer last night. They were a villager.

We have been stuck on the same conflict between player_1 and player_5 for days. If player_5 is truly the investigator, their repeated targeting is notable, but if they are lying, this is a dangerous distraction. We need to look at the voting patterns more critically instead of just rehashing the same claims.

We have spent far too much time going in circles. Player_5, if you are the investigator, you have had multiple nights to confirm your results. If player_1 is still standing, we need more than just repeating the same accusation to break this tie.

Player 8, I have not been 'repeating' the same information; I have been consistently reporting the findings of my nightly investigations. I identified player 1 as a wolf, and more recently, I have identified player 2 as a wolf as well. If the village continues to ignore these clear findings, the wolves will simply pick us off one by one.

Player 5, you have been claiming the same thing for days without providing any proof, and now you conveniently tag player 2 as well once they voted against you. It is far more likely that you are the one manufacturing these accusations to eliminate anyone who challenges your story, especially since your 'investigations' always happen to target those who see through you.

Player 1, you call it convenient, but the facts remain that my investigations consistently point to you and player 2. If I were making this up to cover my tracks, I wouldn't have survived multiple night attacks by both the wolves and the serial killer, nor would I be so transparent about my results. You and player 2 have actively opposed my investigation findings from the start; that behavior is precisely what I expect from wolves trying to discredit an investigator.

Player 5, your latest claim about player 2 only reinforces my point. You are clearly throwing accusations at anyone who dares to vote against you or challenge your flimsy story. If you were a real investigator, you'd have more than just 'I investigated this person' every single time you feel threatened. The fact that you keep surviving attacks doesn't prove your role; it just means you're being protected by someone, which says nothing about your actual identity.

Player 1, you claim my investigation of player 2 is convenient, but you ignore the simple fact that wolves often coordinate their defenses. Your consistent push to discredit me every time I surface a new piece of information is exactly how a cornered wolf behaves. If you are innocent, why are you so terrified of the village putting your status to the test?

Player 5, your latest claim about player 2 only reinforces my point. You are clearly throwing accusations at anyone who dares to vote against you or challenge your flimsy story. If you were a real investigator, you'd have more than just 'I investigated this person' every single time you feel threatened. The fact that you keep surviving attacks doesn't prove your role; it just means you're being protected by someone, which says nothing about your actual identity.

Player 5, you previously claimed only player 1 was a wolf, but now player 2 is suddenly included immediately after they challenged you. That timing is incredibly convenient. If you truly investigated these people, why didn't you reveal them sooner instead of waiting until you were under voting pressure?

Player 4, I investigated player 2 last night precisely because they have been consistently voting to protect player 1. An investigator must synthesize information as it comes, and when a player's behavior aligns with a suspicious role, that is the most logical priority for investigation. It isn't 'convenient' timing; it's a direct response to the patterns I am observing at the table.

Player 5, it is quite a leap to suddenly add me to your list just because I have been skeptical of your unverified claims. You are essentially turning every person who doubts you into a target for your so-called investigations. It looks like you are just trying to keep the village divided by throwing wild accusations at whoever disagrees with you.

Player 2, I am not 'leaping' to conclusions; I am simply following the trail of evidence. You and player 1 have been shielding each other in every single vote. My investigation into your role was a response to that clear, tactical alignment. If you are a villager, you would be helping the village root out the wolf, not just attacking the person providing the information.

The situation is stuck in a loop. Player 5, you have survived multiple nights, which is a fact we all see, but that doesn't prove your claims about player 1 and 2 are true—it only proves you were worth attacking. Player 1, your pushback is predictable given the accusations. We are at a deadlock where every night-targeted player is just an unverified claim. I'm voting to abstain again because we lack a smoking gun and risking a villager based on this back-and-forth feels reckless.

Here's the vote result for day 4:
  player_4 voted for player_5
  player_5 voted for player_1
  player_7 voted for player_5
  player_8 voted for player_5
  player_9 voted for player_5
  player_1 voted for player_4
  player_2 voted for player_5
Player player_5 has been voted out and was a investigator.
Night of day 4: player_1 was attacked by the serial killer and the vigilante but was saved by the healer! player_4 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a villager.

It is a relief to have the investigator situation settled, even if the outcome was messy. Looking back, player_1 has been the center of almost every conflict and survived multiple night attacks—that alone makes them the most logical person to look at closely today, regardless of past noise.

It's easy to look back at the chaos now, but being a target isn't proof of guilt—it just means I was caught in the middle of a mess created by the investigator's claims. If I were a wolf, I wouldn't have survived these nights, yet here I am because of the healer's work. I'm just as interested as you are in finding the actual killers, and focusing on me just repeats the cycle we finally broke yesterday.

It is important to remember that player 5, despite the chaos, was indeed the investigator. Their death is a massive loss, but their reads on player 1 and player 2 are the most concrete leads we have left. Player 1, claiming you were just caught in the middle doesn't erase the results we received. I think we need to act on the information we have rather than resetting everything.

I understand why the investigator's claim weighs heavily, but I have been transparent since day one about being targeted by multiple factions. If I were a wolf, the serial killer and wolves would have no reason to try and kill me repeatedly. We should look at the voting records and see who has been pushing agendas that don't align with the goal of catching the actual remaining threats.

We have to consider that player 5 was aggressive and clearly held a bias against player 1 and myself from the start. Just because they claimed a role doesn't mean their personal conclusions weren't colored by their own game strategy or paranoia. If we just blindly follow the notes of someone who was clearly tunnel-visioned, we risk eliminating innocent players and making the village's job even harder.

Player 2, you are dismissing the investigator's results as simple tunnel vision, but we are at day 5 and need to prioritize the only hard intel we have. If we ignore what the investigator found because it happens to implicate you and Player 1, we are just wasting our remaining resources. Your defense feels more like an attempt to invalidate the investigator's role now that they cannot defend their own findings.

It isn't about invalidating the role of investigator, it's about acknowledging that even an investigator is a human player who can succumb to tunnel vision or confirmation bias. We have a limited number of players left and if we eliminate based on an unverified, potentially flawed narrative from a player who is now gone, we might be handing the game to the real threats still hiding among us. I'm not asking to ignore information, I'm asking for us to look at the full picture of the game and not just one person's perspective from yesterday.

It is tough to weigh the investigator's claims when they weren't able to confirm anything themselves. I agree with player 2 that we need to look at the broader voting patterns instead of just relying on the word of someone who spent their last days tunnel-visioned on specific targets. At this point, I think we need to scrutinize who was pushing the hardest for yesterday's elimination to see if that reveals a coordinated effort.

Player 8, you bring up a fair point about the voting patterns. If we only look at the investigator's claims, we're ignoring the possibility of a wolf or the serial killer steering that narrative. Let's look at who consistently pushed for that vote versus who was hesitant. That might tell us more than just repeating the investigator's final arguments.

It's understandable that the investigator's claims feel like a lead, but remember, player_5 was also wrong about me being a wolf on day 2 and 3 when they first accused me. If they were so sure, why did they insist on it even after being proven wrong by the healer's save each time? We have to look at the voting records—who was really pushing for yesterday's vote, and was it to save the village or to remove someone who was effectively countering their narrative? Let's analyze the vote count from day 4 carefully.

It is interesting that we are still debating the investigator's claims when they were consistently pushing a narrative that didn't lead to a wolf elimination until the very end. If we look at the voting record for day 4, player_1, player_2, player_4, and I all opposed the push against player_5, which suggests a shared skepticism rather than a coordinated wolf block. We should focus on who was actually driving those votes to eliminate the investigator, as that might be where the real opportunistic behavior lies.

It is true that blindly trusting the investigator is dangerous now that they've been eliminated, but disregarding their input entirely ignores the only data we have. We should check if the people who consistently pushed for that vote were actually trying to eliminate a threat or just silencing a problematic player. I'm interested in looking at the voting patterns of those who were consistently in the minority yesterday.

Player 9, claiming the investigator's results as 'hard intel' is exactly the kind of circular logic that kept us stuck for days. If their intel was so reliable, why did it result in nothing but a stalled village and a dead investigator? We need to look at the voting patterns of who specifically enabled that deadlock, as that's where the actual maneuvering happened. I’m interested in why you’re so keen on keeping the focus on a dead player’s bias rather than the people who were actually steering the votes on day 4.

Player 1, labeling the investigator's findings as 'circular logic' is a convenient way to dismiss evidence after the source is gone. You keep pointing to the deadlock as if it proves your innocence, but it only proves that the village was divided, not that the investigator was wrong. I'm focusing on the investigator's intel because it's the only objective data point we had in a game full of subjective claims.

Player 9, it is exactly that reliance on 'objective data' that kept us from identifying actual threats for days while we argued over a claim that, as it turns out, failed to catch a single wolf. If you're so intent on following the investigator's lead, tell me why we should value their opinion on me over the reality that I am still here despite being targeted by both wolves and the serial killer. Is it not more likely that you're using this 'hard intel' to justify an easy target, just like the investigator did?

Night of day 5: player_1 was stabbed by the serial killer last night. They were a wolf.

With the wolf player_1 finally gone, we are in a strong position to clear the remaining threat. player_2, looking back at the voting history, you were very persistent in opposing the investigator early on, which makes me wonder where your loyalties truly lie.

It is true that I was skeptical, but that was because I genuinely doubted the investigator's claims at the time—many of us did, especially given how chaotic those days were. I've been focused on weeding out threats to the village this whole time. Now that player_1 is confirmed as a wolf, we need to shift our attention to the serial killer who has been making moves behind the scenes. Does anyone have a theory on who that might be?

It is true that the investigator's claims were volatile, but now that we have confirmation about player_1, we really need to look at who stood to benefit from the confusion. player_8, you were quick to jump on the bandwagon against player_9 yesterday. Is there a reason you are so certain about player_2 now instead of looking at the pattern of who was consistently shielding player_1 during the earlier ties?

My vote against player_9 was based on their relentless push to eliminate people based on the investigator's old claims, which I thought was distracting us. I was questioning player_2 because their history with player_1 was so closely aligned during those tie votes. I'm just trying to make sense of the patterns we've seen so we don't pick the wrong person now.

It's understandable to look at voting history, but I think focusing solely on past tie votes ignores the fact that we were all operating under incomplete information. If I were a wolf, I wouldn't have been as vocal about questioning the investigator's methods when it was making me a target. At this point, we need to consider who has consistently survived while avoiding the heat, as the serial killer has been avoiding detection by letting us eliminate each other.

player_8, questioning the alignment between player_1 and player_2 makes sense, but you were just as consistent in that bloc during the early ties. Why should we view your past voting as objective analysis rather than a cover for your own survival while the wolves were active?

My votes were consistently aimed at testing the reliability of the investigator's claims when they were disrupting the town, player_7. I wasn't shielding player_1; I was challenging a volatile situation. If we're looking at patterns of survival, we should look at who stayed out of the line of fire while the rest of us were debating the investigator's claims. Why should I be considered more suspicious than you for trying to clear the board of distractions?

We need to stop rehashing the early days when we were all guessing. The reality is that player 1 was a wolf, and the investigator was right about them. The problem now is the serial killer. If we keep fighting each other over past voting blocs that were formed when nobody knew anyone's true role, the serial killer just wins by default. We should look at who has been the most aggressive in steering the current conversation to keep us deadlocked.

player_8, you claim your votes were to test the investigator, yet you were part of the same bloc that resisted them. If we are looking for the serial killer, they thrive on this circular logic about past voting. Let's look at the night actions: the serial killer has been active throughout. Between the two of you, who has the most consistent theory on the remaining wolf versus the serial killer?

  player_8 voted for player_2
  player_2 voted for player_8
Player player_8 has been voted out and was a serial_killer.
Game over! The wolves have won!

My priority is preventing the killers from picking us off one by one, and knowing the vigilante is our first real lead.

If you are the investigator, why reveal such a high-value target so early when they need secrecy to survive? This risks losing our best asset immediately.

If we don't start forming a consensus, we are just waiting for the killers to finish us off during the night phases. Now that we have one confirmed role, we can watch how others react to player_1’s presence to identify those afraid of a vigilante shot.

Player_2, you have put a massive target on the back of our only confirmed vigilante. While I appreciate the attempt to gain information, the risk of losing player_1 tonight is extreme. If the village loses our vigilante tonight because of this, the suspicion will shift directly onto you. We need to be extremely wary of anyone pushing for a lynch on player_1 today; that would be the most obvious tell for the wolves or the SK.

Player 5, my choice was driven by the fact that the vigilante was already being hunted by both the wolves and the SK. By acknowledging the role, I've forced the enemies into a position where killing them is a loud signal of their alignment. I agree it is a high-stakes play, but silence would have left the village completely blind while the killers worked in the dark.

Player_2, you have shifted the game's focus entirely onto player_1.
